whatItIs.text: Shelf-stable tinned fish, most commonly light tuna such as skipjack, packed in water or oil and drained before use.

historyNote.text: The English name came through Spanish atun from Arabic; the nickname Chicken of the Sea stuck so well that in Japan canned tuna is still called shi-chikin, sea chicken.

howToChoose.text: Pick cans that are undented and sealed; water-packed gives a lighter flavour, oil-packed a richer one.

storage.text: Sealed cans keep in the cupboard; once opened, tip the rest into a covered container and refrigerate. The rulebook has the timing.
storage.note: opened-can window lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Fold leftover tuna into pasta, mash with mayonnaise for sandwiches, or crisp into patties with an egg and breadcrumbs.

substitutions.note: richer, softer flakes; swap 1:1 in salads and patties
vegetarian sandwich and salad filling; add lemon and salt
